mainProgression.description: Classic country I-IV-V waltz progression in 3/4 time, the simplest and most foundational progression in country music

sectionProgressions.progression: D - D - G - G - A - A - D - D
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - I - IV - IV - V - V - I - I
sectionProgressions.description: Simple two-bar-per-chord waltz verse allowing the vocal melody to breathe in the 3/4 time feel
Tighter chord changes in the chorus for forward momentum, still in 3/4 waltz time
Simple IV-V-I turnaround connecting sections with a standard country cadence

harmonicFunction: D (I) - Tonic center providing warmth and stability in the waltz feel
G (IV) - Subdominant creating gentle harmonic movement and lift
A (V) - Dominant chord providing tension and resolution back to D
The I-IV-V progression is the absolute bedrock of country music harmony
In 3/4 waltz time, each chord change feels graceful and unhurried
The simplicity of the harmony puts the focus on the lyrical storytelling

techniques.name: Waltz Strumming (3/4 Time)
techniques.description: The essential country waltz strum pattern: strong downstroke on beat 1, lighter strums on beats 2 and 3, creating the characteristic 'OOM-pah-pah' feel

notes: D: X-X-0-2-3-2 (Open D chord)
G: 3-2-0-0-0-3 (Open G chord) or 3-2-0-0-3-3 (Folk G)
A: X-0-2-2-2-0 (Open A chord)
Beat 1: Strong downstroke emphasizing the bass note (root of chord)
Beat 2: Light downstroke or down-up on treble strings
Beat 3: Light downstroke or down-up on treble strings
The pattern creates: BASS-strum-strum (OOM-pah-pah)
sequence: For D chord: Strike the D string (bass root) firmly on beat 1, then light strums on treble strings for beats 2 and 3
For G chord: Strike the low E string (3rd fret, bass root) on beat 1, then light strums on beats 2 and 3
For A chord: Strike the A string (open, bass root) on beat 1, then light strums on beats 2 and 3
Count the iconic vocal hook throughout to maintain the waltz feel
tips: The key to waltz time is making beat 1 clearly stronger than beats 2 and 3
Think of it as heavy-light-light or OOM-pah-pah
Keep your strumming arm swinging in a consistent 3/4 pattern
If coming from 4/4 time songs, practice counting to 3 repeatedly before playing
Listen to classic country waltzes to internalize the feel before attempting the strumming

techniques.name: Basic Open Chords
techniques.description: The three fundamental open chord shapes (D, G, A) used throughout the entire song, making this ideal for absolute beginners

notes: D major: X-X-0-2-3-2 (ring finger 3rd fret B, middle finger 2nd fret high E, index 2nd fret G)
G major: 3-2-0-0-0-3 (middle finger 3rd fret low E, index 2nd fret A, ring finger 3rd fret high E)
A major: X-0-2-2-2-0 (index, middle, ring across 2nd fret of D, G, B strings)
All three chords are in open position using the first three frets
These are the most commonly used chords in all of country music
sequence: Practice each chord individually to get clean sound from all strings
Practice D to G transition: lift all fingers, move to G shape
Practice D to A transition: slide index finger from G string 2nd fret to D string 2nd fret
Practice G to A transition: lift fingers from G shape, form A shape
Chain all transitions: D - G - A - D at slow tempo
tips: Curl your fingers to avoid muting adjacent strings
Press strings firmly just behind the fret wire for clean tone
Check each chord by strumming one string at a time
These three chords will let you play hundreds of country songs
Focus on smooth transitions rather than speed initially

techniques.name: Bass Note Emphasis
techniques.description: Highlighting the root bass note of each chord on beat 1 to create the strong downbeat that defines the waltz feel

notes: D chord: Target the open D string (4th string) as your bass note on beat 1
G chord: Target the 3rd fret of the low E string (6th string) as bass note
A chord: Target the open A string (5th string) as bass note
Beat 1 bass note should be noticeably louder than the strum on beats 2 and 3
The bass note grounds each measure and marks the chord change
sequence: Aim your pick at the bass string of each chord on beat 1
Follow through into a broader strum on beats 2 and 3
Practice isolating just the bass note before adding the strums
The bass note-strum separation creates the waltz character
tips: Think of your pick hand doing two different jobs: bass on 1, strum on 2 and 3
The bass note doesnt need to be isolated perfectly - a slight strum is fine
Start by exaggerating the dynamic difference between beat 1 and beats 2-3
As you get comfortable, the distinction will become natural

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Simple waltz pattern introduction establishing the 3/4 time feel with D major
notes: Sets the waltz tempo at 92 BPM in 3/4 time
Simple open chord strumming establishes the feel
Count: 1-2-3, 1-2-3 throughout
Gentle, unhurried introduction

sections.name: Verse 1
sections.description: First verse with Waylon Jennings' vocals over the easy-going waltz rhythm, two bars per chord
sections.progression: D - D - G - G - A - D
notes: Two bars per chord giving the verse a spacious, waltz-like feel
Strong bass note on beat 1 of each measure
Light strums on beats 2 and 3
Vocal melody sits comfortably within the D major scale

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The memorable chorus with the title lyric, chord changes come slightly faster to build momentum
notes: Chord changes come every bar instead of every two bars
Creates a sense of momentum and arrival for the hook
Strum slightly fuller for the chorus energy
the signature hook is instantly recognizable

sections.name: Verse 2
sections.description: Second verse returning to the spacious two-bars-per-chord pacing
sections.progression: D - D - G - G - A - D
notes: Same structure as verse 1
Willie Nelson joins Waylon for the duet vocal
Maintain the steady waltz rhythm behind the vocal interplay
Keep the dynamics relaxed and easy-going

sections.name: Final Chorus & Outro
sections.description: Final chorus repeating into an extended outro with vocal ad-libs and a gentle fade on D major
sections.progression: D - G - A - D (repeat to fade)
notes: Final chorus with full vocal harmonies between Waylon and Willie
Repeated chorus progression fading gradually
Vocal ad-libs and harmonies over the repeating I-IV-V-I waltz
Song fades out gently on the D major tonic

guitar.recommended: Martin D-28 or similar dreadnought acoustic
alternatives: Fender Telecaster (for electric outlaw country tone)
guitar.pickup: Acoustic preferred; if electric, bridge single-coil for twangy country sound

settings.bass: 5 (balanced low end for waltz bass notes)

effects.distortion: None - clean acoustic or clean electric tone
effects.reverb: Light spring reverb for subtle warmth
effects.other: No effects needed - the simplicity of the tone matches the simplicity of the song

beginner.focus: Learn the three open chords (D, G, A) and the basic waltz strum pattern in 3/4 time
steps: Master open D, G, and A chord shapes until each rings clearly
Learn the waltz strum: strong bass note on 1, light strums on 2 and 3
Practice chord transitions D-G, D-A, G-A slowly in waltz rhythm
Play through the full verse and chorus at slow tempo (60 BPM)

intermediate.focus: Refine the waltz feel with bass note emphasis and add simple fills
steps: Develop distinct bass note targeting on beat 1 for each chord
Add simple hammer-on and pull-off embellishments between chords
Practice at full tempo (92 BPM) with confident chord changes
Work on dynamic control between verse (softer) and chorus (fuller)

advanced.focus: Add Travis picking waltz pattern and develop a complete solo arrangement
steps: Learn a Travis picking adaptation of the waltz pattern
Add simple lead fills between vocal phrases using D major pentatonic
Combine bass, rhythm, and melodic elements for a solo guitar arrangement
Capture the relaxed outlaw country feel of Waylon Jennings' style

commonMistakes: Playing in 4/4 time instead of 3/4 - count to 3 not 4
Making all three beats equal volume - beat 1 must be strongest
Rushing the tempo - this is a relaxed waltz, not a fast song
Overcomplicating the strumming - simplicity is the beauty of this song
Not letting the open chords ring fully between strums
practiceRoutine: Practice counting 1-2-3 while tapping your foot for 2 minutes
Strum open D chord in waltz pattern for 3 minutes (bass-strum-strum)
Practice D-G-A chord transitions in waltz time at 60 BPM
Play through the full song structure at slow tempo
Gradually build to performance tempo of 92 BPM
focusAreas: Strong beat 1 bass note with lighter beats 2 and 3
Smooth chord transitions between D, G, and A
Relaxed strumming arm motion in groups of three
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 3/4 time or accent every third click
Build to performance tempo of 92 BPM
Practice emphasizing beat 1 while keeping 2 and 3 light
